:::{#exm-rct-identification-fails}
#### Without exchangeability, the naive contrast is biased

In the population of @exm-exchangeability-strata,
treatment was not randomized,
so @thm-rct-identification does not apply.
The observed group means are

$$
\ba
\E{Y \mid A = 1}
&= \frac{120 \cdot 10 + 280 \cdot 20}{400}
&& \text{(consistency; average over the treated)} \\
&= \frac{1200 + 5600}{400}
&& \text{(multiply)} \\
&= 17
&& \text{(add and divide)} \\
\E{Y \mid A = 0}
&= 10
&& \text{(consistency; } \E{Y(0) \mid A = 0} = 10 \text{ in that population)}
\ea
$$

so the naive contrast @eq-rct-ate would give $17 - 10 = 7$.
But the treatment raises each patient's mean outcome by exactly 2
in both strata
($10 - 8 = 20 - 18 = 2$),
so the true ATE is 2.
The extra 5 units come from the severe patients' over-representation among the treated:
[confounding](#def-confounding-obs) by $L$.

:::
